sectionsUsed: 4.3.2 The article element: a complete, or self-contained, composition that is in principle independently distributable or reusable (posts, stories, comments). Page claims: article definition, region D, recipe, GIFT o1 reviews.
4.3.3 The section element: a generic section, a thematic grouping of content, typically with a heading. Page claims: section definition, Chef's tips group, Billing group.
4.3.4 The nav element: a section with navigation links, primarily intended for major navigation blocks. Page claims: nav definition, region B, apply distractor d.
4.3.5 The aside element: content tangentially related to the content around it, often a sidebar. Page claims: aside definition, region E, apply distractor b.
4.3.8 The header element: a group of introductory or navigational aids. Page claims: header definition, region A, masthead.

4.3.9 The footer element: a footer for its nearest sectioning content or the body, typically information such as copyright data and related links. Page claims: footer definition, region F, legal line.

4.3.11 Headings and outlines: at least one heading should have heading level 1; each heading following another must have a level less than, equal to, or 1 greater than the previous heading's level. Page claims: outline rules in teach step 3, outline checker, apply question, GIFT o2 items.

4.4.14 The main element: represents the dominant contents of the document; a document must not have more than one main element without the hidden attribute. Page claims: main definition, region C, GIFT o1 one main.

4.4.15 The div element: has no special meaning; authors are encouraged to use it as a last resort when no other element is suitable. Page claims: a div means nothing, keep div for layout-only wrappers.

Content sectioning: header, nav, main, article, section, aside and footer described as the elements that organize document content into logical pieces and landmarks. Page claims: the seven-element list.

Document conformance requirements for use of ARIA attributes in HTML: header maps to role banner when not inside article, aside, main, nav or section; nav to navigation; main to main; footer to contentinfo under the same scoping rule. Page claims: prediction explanation that these elements expose landmark roles.
